strengths: Significance: Repeated parametric MIP solving is an important application. Adding two cardinality constraints provides a simple interface to commercial solvers, and exhaustively solving the four complementary regions preserves global optimality independently of prediction quality.

Empirical merit: Experiments cover knapsack, set covering, and IEEE-118-based unit commitment using Gurobi and COPT. Figure 1 reports substantial time-to-target improvements, including with default solver heuristics, suggesting practical value as a primal heuristic.

Originality and presentation: Using concentration inequalities to choose aggregate prediction-error budgets offers an interpretable perspective on prediction-guided search. Algorithm 1 clearly communicates the core construction.

Limitations and ethics: Remark 6 candidly acknowledges unrealistic posterior assumptions, and Section 4.4 discusses infeasibility and parameter sensitivity. The synthetic and benchmark experiments raise no evident material ethical concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness: The central guarantee in Theorem 2 is not established. The sets U and L depend on test-instance predictions, but Appendix B.4 applies Hoeffding using unconditional correctness probabilities as though these sets were fixed. A3 does not establish the required conditional means or independence after selection. Separately, Appendix B.1's factorization from equation (3) to (4) is invalid: independent training datasets do not make errors independent after averaging over a shared test instance. These gaps undermine the claimed theoretical justification.

Connection between theory and implementation: Theorem 3 assumes exact conditional means and independent solution coordinates; independence of predictor outputs does not establish these properties. Section 4.1 trains all coordinate models on the same dataset and uses some SCP labels obtained at a 10% optimality gap. There is no calibration or joint coverage evaluation connecting these predictions to the guarantees. Moreover, Section 4.2 uses delta = 0.8, which gives only a 20% per-inequality confidence lower bound even under the idealized assumptions.

Evaluation: Section 4.2 measures time to an objective selected by PreMIO's own 120-second run. Without matched-budget objective gaps, primal progress curves, and explicit handling of unreached targets, these ratios provide incomplete evidence of practical acceleration. Testing uses only 20 instances per MKP/SCP configuration and five per SCUC configuration, without uncertainty estimates. Evaluation of certified solving is limited to 20 knapsack instances.

MIPLIB evidence: Section 4.4 excludes infeasible restricted problems and cases where both methods time out, retaining 57 of 132 instances. The reported 16% improvement therefore describes an outcome-selected subset. A full-suite evaluation should include failures and fallback costs. Table 3 also lists only 30 entries, including a duplicated blp-ar98, rather than documenting all 57 retained instances.

Originality: The incremental contribution over prediction-based neighborhoods and local branching remains insufficiently isolated. The manuscript acknowledges related prediction-distance cuts [11] and local branching [12], but compares neither against these approaches nor against simpler confidence-based fixing or empirically tuned cardinality budgets. Consequently, the benefit specifically attributable to the proposed concentration-based construction is unclear.

Presentation and methodological consistency: Appendix D defines alpha_L and alpha_U as misclassification rates but calls them accuracies and proposes maximizing them. It then selects tau approximately 0.1 despite specifying tau in [0.5, 1). Section 3.2 also reverses the pruning condition: if the preferred region excludes every global optimum, at least one complementary branch must remain feasible under the incumbent objective cutoff. These inconsistencies affect implementation and interpretation.

Reproducibility: The manuscript lacks a code/data artifact link, exact solver versions, random seeds, logistic-regression fitting details, and training/inference overhead measurements. Numerical summaries also need reconciliation: applying Section 4.2's shift-10 geometric mean to Table 1's displayed left-hand timings gives approximately 36.6 and 32.1 seconds, rather than the reported 28.7 and 25.8.
